name: Vakanssi: Careers Page, Hiring & Applicant Tracking
author: Vakanssi

sections.description:
Vakanssi is a recruitment plugin and complete applicant tracking system (ATS) for WordPress. Post your openings on a careers page or job board on your own site and run the whole hiring process there.

It brings branded job listings with Google-for-Jobs structured data, a native application form, an applications inbox with a configurable drag-and-drop pipeline board, templated emails, and tools for handling candidate data (export, erasure and scheduled retention), all on your own server, with no per-seat SaaS fees.

A complete hiring workflow:

  • Jobs & careers: a vakanssi_job post type, a branded careers archive (at /jobs/ by default, or on your own careers page) and [vakanssi_jobs] shortcode, and valid Google-for-Jobs JobPosting structured data that is withheld automatically when a job is not eligible (expired, no location, no apply path, …).

  • Application intake: a native application form with a secure CV upload (type-verified by magic bytes, randomised filename, owner-only permissions), spam/honeypot/rate-limiting, and candidate de-duplication by email.

  • Applications inbox & pipeline board: a sortable, filterable inbox plus a build-free React Kanban board with a candidate profile drawer; configurable stages; bulk move/delete.

  • Interviews & calendar invites: schedule an interview from the candidate’s record and send a real .ics invite that Google, Outlook and Apple render as an actionable event, with no OAuth and no connected account. Reschedule, cancel, and keep internal notes that reach your interviewers’ calendars and never the candidate’s.

  • Application data & export: export applications to CSV, print or save any application as a PDF, and edit application details, right from the inbox.

  • Email: templated confirmation/recruiter/rejection/offer emails with personalization tags and an SMTP-compatible sender, logged and de-duplicated.

  • Candidate data controls: consent capture, WordPress core data export/erase integration (with a complete cascade across all candidate data), a retention-purge cron, and an audit log. These are tools you operate; they do not by themselves make a site compliant with any particular law.

  • Blocks, page builders & themes: a Job Listings block for the block editor, native Elementor widgets for the listing, the application form and the job details (Elementor Pro Theme Builder archive/single templates are respected too), a Divi module, and shortcodes for everywhere else. Block themes on WordPress 6.7 and later get editable Site Editor templates; classic themes get the built-in archive.

  • First-run setup wizard: sender identity and a careers page in a few clicks, with optional sample content and a prompt to post your first job.

  • AI assistants: on WordPress 6.9 and later, with the free MCP Adapter plugin, an AI assistant such as Claude can list your jobs, read one and draft a new one. It signs in as one of your users and can do only what that user may do, and drafts are never published on their own.

  • Foundations: scale-ready custom tables (engineered for 10k+ applications), a modular architecture (disabled modules load no code/assets), capability-based roles (Recruiter, Hiring Manager, HR/Compliance), and a vakanssi/v1 REST API with per-route permission checks.

External services

Vakanssi does not contact any external service on its own. Everything it stores stays on your server. One optional integration talks to a third party, and only after you switch it on and enter your own credentials:

Cloudflare Turnstile (optional spam protection for the public application form)

Turnstile is off by default. It activates only once you enter a Turnstile site key and secret under Hiring → Settings → Application form. While it is enabled:

  • each visitor’s browser loads the challenge script from https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js;

  • when someone submits an application, the resulting challenge token, the visitor’s IP address and your secret key are sent to https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify so Cloudflare can confirm the submission is not automated;

  • when an administrator uses “Test these keys” on the settings screen, that admin’s browser loads the same challenge script, and the resulting token, the admin’s IP address and the secret key being tested are sent to the same address, so the key pair can be checked without waiting for a real application.

No application content (no name, email, CV, or answers) is sent to Cloudflare. Turning the setting off stops all contact with the service.

Service: https://www.cloudflare.com/products/turnstile/
Terms of service: https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/
Privacy policy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the vakanssi folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install through the Plugins screen.

  2. Activate the plugin. Activation creates the database tables, installs roles, provisions protected file storage, and opens a short setup wizard.

  3. Complete Hiring → Setup (sender email, careers page), post your first job, then review Hiring → Tools → Status for system status.
sections.faq:
Does removing the plugin delete my candidate data?

No. Uninstalling removes roles, capabilities, and plugin settings, but your hiring data is kept unless you explicitly enable Hiring → Settings → General → Delete all data on uninstall. While another copy of Vakanssi is still installed (for example in a second plugin folder), deleting a copy removes nothing, so the copy you keep runs with its settings and data.

Are uploaded CVs protected from direct download?

Yes, with defence in depth. Candidate files are stored in a protected vakanssi folder in your uploads directory, under random 128-bit file names, with an Apache deny rule, index guards and a generated Nginx rule. Vakanssi then verifies over HTTP that the folder is not directly reachable, and shows an admin warning (with the exact Nginx rule to add) if it is. The plugin itself only serves CVs through an authenticated, permission-checked download link. To keep them outside your public site entirely, define VAKANSSI_STORAGE_DIR as an absolute path in wp-config.php; moving your existing CVs is covered at https://docs.vakanssi.com/admin/move-cv-storage/

Who on my team can see candidate applications and CVs?

Anyone you grant a hiring role to. Vakanssi ships three roles (Recruiter, Hiring Manager, and HR / Compliance) plus Administrator, and any user with the “view applications” capability can see every candidate and download every CV in the pipeline. In other words, Vakanssi does not restrict staff to only the jobs or candidates assigned to them: it assumes your hiring team is trusted, which is the right default for most small teams. Only grant these roles to people who should see all applicants.

How do I report a security issue?

Email security@vakanssi.com rather than posting in the support forum, so a fix can ship before the details are public. Please include the Vakanssi version, your WordPress and PHP versions, and steps to reproduce. You will get an acknowledgement within three business days and an initial assessment within a week, and you will be credited in the changelog for the release that fixes it unless you would rather not be. Only the most recent release receives security fixes, so updating is always part of the answer.

What personal data is included in a GDPR data-export request?

When you run Tools → Export Personal Data for a candidate’s email, Vakanssi includes their profile (name, email, phone, location), every application (position, stage, status, date, and whether consent was given), the cover letter, their LinkedIn profile, each uploaded CV/attachment (the file itself, with its filename and upload date), the submission context stored with the application (the page the application was sent from), the recruiter notes and interview notes written about them, their interviews, and the emails Vakanssi sent them. Other details stored with an application or the candidate are included too, under “Additional application data”. The export deliberately does not name the staff member who wrote a note, gave a rating, or conducted an interview. That is a third party’s personal data, not the candidate’s.

The matching Erase Personal Data tool removes all of it, including the CV files on disk. Export and erasure share one list of the tables that hold notes, interviews and emails about a candidate, so the two stay in step.

Does it work on WordPress multisite?

Yes, activated per site or network-wide. Each site keeps its own jobs, candidates, CVs and settings (data is never shared between sites), and each site chooses independently whether deleting the plugin also deletes its hiring data. There is no network-level configuration screen; settings are per site.

Network activation is the recommended setup: deleting a site then removes that site’s Vakanssi data with it, and if some of its CVs cannot be deleted, Vakanssi keeps the list of those files. With per-site activation, a site deleted where Vakanssi is not active keeps its Vakanssi tables, and its CVs when they are in a custom storage folder. Since 1.3.0 a super admin sees this data in Site Health and under Hiring → Tools → Data, and removes it there after a confirmation. When Vakanssi cannot prove a site’s CV files are gone (for example a folder it cannot read), it keeps that site’s file list and says why. A single site turned into a network keeps finding the CVs it stored before, and Site Health names the folder to move them from.

Does it work on Nginx?

Yes. Nginx ignores .htaccess, so add the generated location block to your server config. The plugin’s screens show the rule, and Site Health flags the folder, when it is reachable.

Does it work with my theme and page builder?

Yes, and you do not have to fall back to a shortcode. The block editor gets a Job Listings block. Elementor gets three native widgets (the listing, the application form, and the job details) grouped under a Vakanssi section in the panel, and they work with the free Elementor; if you run Elementor Pro, your Theme Builder archive and single templates for jobs are used instead of ours. Divi gets a Jobs module. Shortcodes ([vakanssi_jobs], [vakanssi_job_apply], [vakanssi_job_details]) still work anywhere else, including builders with no dedicated integration.

Themes need nothing special. Block themes on WordPress 6.7 and later get editable “Jobs archive” (while the archive page is on) and “Single job” templates in the Site Editor, built from your own header and footer; classic themes get the built-in archive. The candidate-facing pages are styled so they survive a theme’s own CSS reset, so the listing and the apply button look the same whichever theme you run.

Can I restyle the careers/job pages, and will custom CSS slow my site down?

Yes. Under Hiring → Settings → Jobs & Careers → Appearance you can turn off Vakanssi’s front-end stylesheet entirely, if your theme styles the markup. For your own styling, use WordPress’s built-in editor at Appearance → Customize → Additional CSS, which adds no extra request. Vakanssi keeps its own selectors as light as theme-proofing allows and its class names stable. Match their weight, such as .vakanssi-apply-form .vakanssi-apply-button for the application form’s Submit button or :root p.vakanssi-apply a.vakanssi-apply-button for a job’s Apply link, and style :hover, :focus and :active as well, since Vakanssi sets those too. On most pages that is enough without !important.

The same vakanssi- class names are on the careers and job pages under block themes and classic themes alike, so one rule covers both. On a block theme your theme keeps control of the spacing, and Vakanssi sets only the column the careers page, the jobs archive and a job share: override it with .vakanssi-careers-page { --wp--style--global--content-size: 1100px; --wp--style--global--wide-size: 1100px; } (the same on .vakanssi-careers-archive and .vakanssi-single-job). The job list keeps a 960px reading width inside that column; add --vakanssi-measure: 1100px; to the same rule to widen the list too.

Do I need any special server setup for a production site?

Two things are worth doing on a live hiring site, and both are standard WordPress production hygiene rather than Vakanssi requirements. First, switch WordPress to a real cron trigger: out of the box, WordPress runs scheduled tasks only when someone visits your site, so on a quiet careers site scheduled work can run late. Vakanssi relies on it to purge candidate data once its retention period is up. Add define( 'DISABLE_WP_CRON', true ); to wp-config.php and trigger wp-cron.php every few minutes; most managed hosts offer this as a checkbox. Second, if your host offers a persistent object cache (Redis or Memcached), enable it: Vakanssi uses transients for its dashboard counters, and an object cache keeps those out of the database under heavy traffic. Apply-form rate limits always use the database, so they hold either way. Nothing breaks without either step.

Can I disable the /jobs/ archive page?

Yes: Hiring → Settings → Jobs & Careers → Job URLs → “Archive page”. Single job pages stay live under your job URL base (e.g. /jobs/job-title/); the archive URL becomes available for your own page, such as a Careers page using the [vakanssi_jobs] shortcode.

What stops two recruiters overwriting each other on the board?

Every save carries the state the screen was showing when you started editing. If someone else changed that candidate first, the save is refused and you are shown what changed instead of quietly losing one of the two edits. This runs over ordinary REST requests, so it needs nothing special on your server and works on any host that runs WordPress normally.

Can I switch from another job or recruitment plugin?

Yes. The free Import tool copies jobs and applications from WP Job Openings and Simple Job Board, and jobs from WP Job Manager (its core plugin has no applications). It never changes or deletes the originals, so you can keep the old plugin running until you are happy with the result. You can also import jobs from a CSV file.

Is Vakanssi a job board plugin?

It is a job board for your own organisation: your openings on a careers page on your own site, with the applications that come in managed in the same place. It is not a multi-employer board where other companies sign up and post their own jobs.

Can I use Vakanssi with an AI assistant?

Yes, on WordPress 6.9 and later. Install the free MCP Adapter plugin and connect an assistant that supports MCP (such as Claude or Cursor) with an application password. It can then list your jobs, read one and create a draft, with the same permissions as the user it signs in as. Vakanssi itself contacts no AI service: your assistant connects to your site.

None of these abilities read applications or CVs.

Is there a Pro version?

Yes. Vakanssi Pro is a separate plugin, coming soon, for teams that need more. Everything in this plugin stays free and fully working. Get notified when it launches at https://vakanssi.com/#notify
sections.changelog:
1.3.20

  • Improved: form fields on the careers page and the application form now have a light outline with a clear bottom edge, so the form looks calmer while every field stays easy to see.
  • Changed: the “Apply for this position” button under a job’s title is now off by default. If you never changed this setting, the button no longer shows after this update; turn it back on under Hiring → Settings → Jobs & Careers, “Apply button at the top”. The application form further down the page is unchanged.

1.3.19

  • New: AI assistants connected through the WordPress Abilities API (WordPress 6.9+, with the MCP Adapter plugin) can list jobs, read a job and create a job draft. Drafts are never published, and scripts are stripped from the text.
  • Improved: sample data now includes CVs, ratings, notes, an interview, email history and activity, so the board looks lived in.
  • Fixed: on dark themes the careers list, job page and their links were nearly invisible (job titles at 1.17:1). Text on the page now follows the theme’s own text colour, keyboard focus rings included, and on light themes nothing changes.
  • Fixed: on light themes with a tinted background, grey and brand-colour text on the careers page now reads at 4.5:1 or better, whatever brand colour is set.
  • Fixed: moving an application into a stage from another job’s pipeline is now refused.

1.3.18

  • Fixed: when someone applied again at the same moment their application, person or data was deleted, erased or purged, the new details or the whole application could be left behind or attached to nobody. Every write onto an existing application or person now waits for, or is refused by, a delete in progress.
  • Fixed: deleting or erasing a person while they applied again no longer leaves their new application and CV attached to no one, and a returning applicant can no longer be told their application arrived when it was not saved.
  • Fixed: a LinkedIn URL typed on a new application that differs from the one on file is shown in the “Submitted with different details” note and included in the personal data export.
  • Fixed: the personal data export now includes the star rating staff gave each application.
  • Fixed: importing from Simple Job Board copies only the applicant’s own CV, never another applicant’s file named in a form field.
  • Fixed: “Remove all applicant data” no longer says “0 stored file(s) could not be removed” when the storage folder was already gone.
  • Developers: Transaction::after_commit() runs a callback after the outermost commit; vakanssi/application/deleted and its audit row now fire only once a delete has committed.
